name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3385: Konyo saw two grokbot accounts in the fleet. MEASURED the same minute: BOTH are real seats that belong there - grok-bot-vm-346371813 on v3383 online, and cursor on v3377 offline since 03:37 - the Linux native seat and the Cursor guest seat. Nothing may be merged or pruned; the defect is that the rail could not tell him WHICH IS WHICH. And the install id is IDENTICAL on both (1bba07477e40), so disambiguating by install would still have drawn two identical lines and looked right doing it: machine is the only field that differs. It matters more since v3384, where the peer VERSION decides whether item names can be published, so two rows reading GrokBot hid which seat was the stale one. FOUR sites rendered this label independently - the stale list, two tooltips and the rail row - so the fix is one _fleetName helper they all call, not four edits. Only the AMBIGUOUS case changes: a nickname owned by one machine renders exactly as before, an unnamed row still falls back to its machine, and a row with neither is a question mark. 6 cases that RUN the shipped helper in node rather than re-implementing it, 3 red-proofs PROVEN, 496 gates, plus a heart row in all four registries that counts shared nicknames in the live roster and names the versions they sit on.
